### Goal

Implement a feature that wire the guest post from GitHub Discussions into our website. It needs to connect the post to a specific episode (can ask us which episode a post shall link to) and reflect that on "Graph View" feature on our current website.

### Why

We want to have a workflow to ship blog post currently located in Github Discussion to a dedicated place on our website.

### Success criteria

- [ ] Set up a workflow to ship blog post from Github Discussion to a dedicated place on our website
- [ ] Match the post page style to the style of our current episode page but higlight its authors (not our team members). 
- [ ] Make sure "Guest Post_ CongJie Pan_The Human Measure: AI Needs Personalization Beyond "One-Size-Fits-All" #46" shown up nicely

### Current strategy

You can use a giscus-style API and then render the post

### Subgoals or child tasks

_No response_

### Related work

_No response_

### Suggested first Sepo action

_No response_

Here's my plan for wiring the guest post into the site. Since you pinged with no extra instructions, I'm staying in **plan-only mode** — I'll wait for your go-ahead (and the answers to the questions at the bottom) before writing code.

## What I found

This is a [Quartz v4](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz/) static site. The relevant machinery:

- **Episode pages** live in [`content/episodes/*.md`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/tree/main/content/episodes) with frontmatter `title`, `episodeId`, `date`, `coverImage`, `youtubeUrl`, `guestOffset`, `tags`.
- **Series rendering** is in [`quartz/components/pages/Content.tsx`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/main/quartz/components/pages/Content.tsx). The `isSeriesPage` check is **hardcoded to the `episodes/` and `livestreams/` prefixes** — it injects the YouTube embed, renders the inline header (`episode-id · title · date`), and hides the default page header. A new content type won't get this styling unless we extend that check.
- **Cards / guest name**: [`EpisodeCarousel.tsx`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/main/quartz/components/EpisodeCarousel.tsx) shows `tags[0]` as the guest name, positioned via `guestOffset`. Carousels + sidebar lists are wired per-section in [`quartz.layout.ts`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/main/quartz.layout.ts).
- **Graph View** ([`quartz/components/Graph.tsx`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/main/quartz/components/Graph.tsx)) is built from `[[wikilinks]]` / backlinks between pages. So "reflect on Graph View" = the post must wikilink to the episode (and ideally an author page), and the episode should link back.
- **People pages** ([`content/people/*.md`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/tree/main/content/people)) use an `## Appearances` section that wikilinks to episodes — this is the existing pattern for connecting a person into the graph.
- **The target post**: discussion [#46](https://github.com/orgs/augmented-mind/discussions/46) by **CongJie-Pan** ("The Human Measure…"). It explicitly references **Episode 01** (Omar Shaikh), and embeds 4 images hosted on `hackmd.io` (external hotlinks — fragile, should be localized).

## Proposed approach

Create a **dedicated `content/guest-posts/` section** that reuses the episode page chrome but highlights the *external author* instead of treating them like a team-member guest tag.

1. **Content + slug**: new `content/guest-posts/` folder (slug `guest-posts/`), plus a `guest-posts/index.md` list page. Convert discussion #46 → `content/guest-posts/the-human-measure.md`. Frontmatter would add an `author` field (e.g. `author: "CongJie Pan"`, `authorUrl: https://congjie-pan.github.io/`) and a `coverImage`.
2. **Author highlight**: extend `Content.tsx` `isSeriesPage` (or add a parallel `isGuestPost` branch) so the inline header reads e.g. `GUEST POST · author name · date` with the author styled prominently (distinct from team-member styling). No YouTube embed for posts.
3. **Graph wiring**: add `[[ep01]]` wikilink in the post body where it references Episode 01, and add an `## Appearances`-style backlink. Optionally create `content/people/congjie-pan.md` so the author becomes its own graph node.
4. **Images**: download the 4 hackmd.io images into `quartz/static/guest-posts/` and rewrite the markdown to point at local paths (avoids hotlink breakage + privacy leakage). Same for a cover image.
5. **Discovery**: add a guest-posts sidebar list + landing carousel entry in `quartz.layout.ts`, mirroring the episodes/livestreams pattern.
6. **The "workflow" piece**: a small Node script (`scripts/fetch-guest-post.ts`) that takes a discussion number, pulls it via the GitHub GraphQL Discussions API, and scaffolds the markdown + downloads images. Whether this also becomes a GitHub Action (auto-run on a labeled discussion) vs. a manual `npm run fetch-guest-post 46` depends on your answer below.

## Step-by-step execution (once approved)

1. Build the fetch script and run it against #46 to scaffold the markdown + localize images.
2. Hand-clean the generated markdown (reference list, episode wikilink, frontmatter).
3. Extend `Content.tsx` + `custom.scss` for the guest-post header/author styling.
4. Add author page + episode backlink for graph connectivity.
5. Wire sidebar list + carousel in `quartz.layout.ts`.
6. Build locally (`npx quartz build --serve`), verify the post renders, the author is highlighted, and the node appears connected to EP01 in Graph View.

## Questions before I start

1. **Episode link** — #46 references **Episode 01 (Omar Shaikh)**. Link the post to `ep01`, correct? Or a different episode?
2. **Workflow scope** — do you want a full **GitHub Action** that auto-publishes when a discussion is labeled (e.g. `guest-post`), or is a **manually-run script** enough for now? (Auto-publishing from discussions adds review/safety considerations I'd want to scope carefully.)
3. **Dedicated place** — is `/guest-posts/` the URL/section you want, surfaced as its own sidebar list + landing carousel like Episodes? Or nested under episodes?
4. **Author node** — OK to create a `content/people/congjie-pan.md` page so the author shows as a distinct Graph node, or just inline byline + external link?
5. **Images** — OK to localize the hackmd.io images into the repo's `static/` (recommended), and do you have a preferred **cover image** for the post's card?

---
`claude` | `default` | `high` | `GitHub Actions 1000001764`

- Branch: `agent/implement-issue-71/claude-27077733334`
- Pull request: https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/pull/73

Implemented issue #71 by adding a dedicated `content/guest-posts/` section and wiring GitHub Discussion #46 (CongJie Pan, "The Human Measure") into the site. `Content.tsx` now renders a guest-post header that highlights the external author (badge + title + byline linking to their site) instead of treating them as a team-member guest, reusing the episode page's card chrome; `quartz.layout.ts` suppresses the default title/meta for guest posts and adds a sidebar list + landing-page carousel; `custom.scss` extends the episode card styling to `guest-posts/`. The post links to `[[ep01]]`, which resolves to an internal link so it appears connected to Episode 01 in Graph View (with a matching backlink on the EP01 page). The 4 hackmd.io images were localized into `quartz/static/guest-posts/the-human-measure/`. A reusable importer (`scripts/import-guest-post.mjs`, `npm run import:guest-post`) fetches a discussion via the GraphQL API, downloads its images, and scaffolds the markdown. Verified with a full `quartz build` (clean, 84 files emitted): the post renders with the author-highlight header, no duplicate title, localized images, and a bidirectional graph link to EP01. `tsc` shows only 7 pre-existing errors (0 introduced); new files pass Prettier.
